chunks: Muhammad ibn Bakran al-Naqqash and Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Mu'addib (may God be pleased with them) narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hamdani, from Ali ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from his father, who said: I asked Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the night of the middle of Sha'ban.

He said: It is a night in which God frees slaves from the Fire and forgives major sins. I said: Is there any specific prayer for it in addition to other nights? He said: There is no appointed (specific) prayer for it, but if you wish to volunteer in it with something, then perform the Prayer of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), and increase in it the remembrance of God, the Exalted, and seeking forgiveness and supplication, for my father (peace be upon him) used to say: Supplication is answered on that night. I said to him: The people say that it is the Night of 'Sikkak'. He said (peace be upon him): That is the Night of Power (Qadr) in the month of Ramadan.

key_terms.صَلَاةُ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ: The Prayer of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ النِّصْفِ مِنْ شَعْبَانَ: The Night of the Middle of Sha'ban
key_terms.يُعْتِقُ اللَّهُ فِيهَا الرِّقَابَ مِنَ: God frees slaves from the Fire

ai.seo_question: What are the virtues and recommended acts for the Night of Mid-Sha'ban according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates the Night of Mid-Sha'ban as a pivotal occasion for divine emancipation from Hellfire and the forgiveness of major sins, emphasizing that while no specific prayer is mandated, the voluntary Prayer of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib is highly recommended alongside abundant supplication. He further clarifies a prevalent scholarly distinction by identifying 'Laylat al-Sikkak' not with this night, but with Laylat al-Qadr in Ramadan, thereby resolving common confusions in popular piety. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on voluntary acts of worship and the specific spiritual efficacy of supplication during this blessed night.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 28-44 Muhammad ibn Bakran al-Naqqash and Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Mu’addib - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hamdani quoted on the authority of Ali ibn Al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Fadhdhal, on the authority of his father, “I asked Ali ibn Musa Al-Ridha (s) about the night of the middle of Sha’ban.

The Imam (s) said, “It is the night to get released from the Fire. On that night major sins will be forgiven.” I said, “Are there any additional prayers for that night?” The Imam (s) said, “It does not have any especial prayers. However, if you like to do a recommendable act on that nightyou can say the Ja’far ibn Abi Talib’s Prayer and mention the Honorable the Exalted God, ask for forgiveness and supplicate a lot. My father (s) said, ‘Supplications are accepted (fulfilled) on that night.’ I said, “The people say that that night is the night of ‘Sekak.“ The Imam (s) said, “That is the Night of Power (‘Qadr) in the (Arabic) month of Ramadan.”
